page: Microsoft Azure L12aos_v4 is a storage-oriented virtual machine belonging to the Laosv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 96.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 8639 GB of local capacity and is Premium Storage capable. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the L12aos_v4 demonstrates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing and text generation for small LLM models also rank in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores, falls within the average range. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in memory bandwidth; while read-only cached small block bandwidth is average, the read-only uncached large block memory bandwidth is weak, falling into the bottom 25%.

Given its high local storage capacity of 8639 GB and a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the L12aos_v4 offers high resource density for storage-heavy workloads. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for applications requiring large local scratch space or high-capacity databases without the overhead of external storage attachments. The instance is well-suited for database operations, text processing, software compilation, and moderate-scale web serving, though workloads requiring high uncached memory bandwidth may experience bottlenecks.
description: Microsoft Azure L12aos_v4 is a storage-focused virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs, 96.0 GB of RAM, and a substantial 8639 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers strong single-core CPU and text processing performance, placing in the top 25% of benchmarks. However, its uncached large-block memory read bandwidth is a notable tradeoff, ranking in the bottom 25%. With a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and massive local storage, the L12aos_v4 is highly suited for database operations, large-scale text processing, and storage-intensive workloads.
